sources.note: A three-pass formal proof document establishing a relative/conditional KnowledgeOS Kernel minimality theorem. Pass 1 proves a capability-irreducibility lemma and a first minimality theorem using a pointwise-observation semantic equivalence; a critical second-pass review finds the equivalence definition underspecified (Obs as placeholder) and the irreducibility lemma universally too weak (single tested witness, not all admissible alternatives); pass 3 repairs both with trace equivalence over admissible histories and a genuinely universal irreducibility definition, proving the corrected final theorem (A1-A5 assumptions: fixed contract, fixed trace observables, trace equivalence, completeness, irreducibility => no strictly-smaller complete semantically-equivalent kernel exists). Resolves the DetectGap-derivability and two-13-operator-minima puzzles, excludes Zero/Representation/truth-manufacture from the primitive kernel, and produces a six-way Kernel/Representation/Reasoning-Regime/Zero-Lens/Governance/Execution DDD boundary plus a closed twelve-step proof-construction pipeline.

rows.anchor: The wrong theorem would be |K|=13 ... The correct theorem is: Among candidate implementations satisfying a fixed semantic contract, invariant-preservation requirement, transition requirement, and observable-behaviour requirement, no implementation can remove an irreducible required epistemic capabil
rows.statement: States the actual theorem to be proved: not that KnowledgeOS has exactly 13 kernel operators, but that among implementations satisfying a fixed semantic contract, no implementation can remove an irreducible required epistemic capability without losing semantic completeness, formalized as K_min=min_preceq{K: K|=C_KOS} ordered by semantic capability inclusion, not operator count.

rows.anchor: A capability is defined as: c in C iff there exists an admissible epistemic scenario in which the presence or absence of c produces a difference in contract-observable behaviour. ... operator decomposition != semantic capability decomposition.
rows.statement: Defines a capability c as belonging to the required set C iff there exists an admissible scenario where its presence or absence produces a difference in contract-observable behaviour, establishing that operator decomposition (how many named functions implement something) is not the same as semantic capability decomposition (which distinct behaviors are required).

rows.anchor: E_t --Gamma--> A_t where E_t = epistemic state, A_t = attributed epistemic state. We do not define K_t=Gamma(E_t,...) and simultaneously require Knows(p)=>True(p) without truth entering the construction. ... the factive predicate remains externally constrained: Knows(a,p,c,t) => True(p,c,t) while A_
rows.statement: Separates epistemic attribution (A_t=Gamma(E_t,Q_t,C_t,EC_t), an internal kernel transformation) from the externally-constrained factive predicate Knows(a,p,c,t)=>True(p,c,t), preventing the kernel from manufacturing truth merely by attribution and thereby preventing the minimality proof from hiding truth verification inside the kernel.

rows.anchor: K1 ==_sem K2 iff for every admissible (q,c,e,x), the two implementations produce observationally indistinguishable semantic behaviour: Obs(K1,q,c,e,x)=Obs(K2,q,c,e,x). Obs = (State,Gap,Determination,Revision,History,InvariantStatus,Attribution,Transition). ... internal representations may differ ...
rows.statement: Defines the first-pass semantic equivalence K1 ==_sem K2 as pointwise equality of an eight-component observation function (State, Gap, Determination, Revision, History, InvariantStatus, Attribution, Transition) across every admissible situation, establishing that two kernels can have different internal representations while being semantically equivalent -- 'this is the missing mathematical piece that previously prevented a genuine minimality theorem.'

rows.anchor: Lemma 1 -- Capability Irreducibility. Let c in C_K. Suppose there exists an admissible scenario s_c such that Obs(s_c|c)=1 but Obs(s_c|C_K\{c})=0. Then c is irreducible with respect to the declared capability basis. Proof: Assume the contrary ... Obs(s_c|C_K\{c})=Obs(s_c|c) ... Contradiction. Theref
rows.statement: Proves Lemma 1 (Capability Irreducibility): if there exists an admissible scenario where capability c produces an observable effect that the remaining capability set cannot reproduce, then c cannot be removed from the declared capability basis, via a proof by contradiction against the assumption that c is derivable from the rest.

rows.anchor: Theorem 1 -- Minimal Capability Set. If for every proper subset S' subsetneq S there exists an admissible witness w_S' such that Obs(K_S,w_S') != Obs(K_S',w_S'), then S is a minimal semantically complete capability set. Proof: ... contradiction ... Hence S is minimal.
rows.statement: Proves a first-pass Theorem 1 (Minimal Capability Set): given a semantically complete capability set S such that every proper subset S' has an admissible witness distinguishing K_S from K_S', S is minimal, via a proof by contradiction assuming some proper subset were also complete.

rows.anchor: the earlier exhaustive search found: the original 13-operator C0 was inadequate; adding Qualify repaired the missing capability; DetectGap was derivable; ... exactly two minimal implementations appeared; both had 13 operators; the difference was packaging. That gives strong experimental evidence ...
rows.statement: Explains why the earlier exhaustive 13-operator search (finding the original C0 inadequate, Qualify repairing a missing capability, DetectGap derivable, and exactly two minimal 13-operator packagings differing only in packaging) constitutes strong experimental evidence for a candidate lower bound but does not by itself prove universal minimality -- experimentally irreducible implies candidate lower bound, never a universal theorem.

rows.anchor: Suppose the irreducible capability set is C_irr={c_1,...,c_m}. By Lemma 1: for all c_i in C_irr, c_i not-preceq C_irr\{c_i}. Therefore every semantically complete kernel must realize each c_i: C_irr subseteq Capabilities(K) for every admissible kernel K. Hence |C_irr| <= |Capabilities(K)| for every
rows.statement: Derives the lower-bound argument: since Lemma 1 shows every member of an irreducible capability set C_irr cannot be derived from the rest, every semantically complete kernel must realize all of C_irr, giving C_irr subseteq Capabilities(K) and hence |C_irr|<=|Capabilities(K)| for every admissible implementation K.

rows.anchor: Now construct a reference kernel K* = Implementation(C_irr). If we demonstrate K* |= {semantic adequacy, transition completeness, invariant preservation, capability completeness, observable behaviour contract} then |Capabilities(K*)|=|C_irr|. Combined with the lower bound ... K* is capability-minima
rows.statement: Constructs the matching upper bound: a reference kernel K*=Implementation(C_irr) that, if shown to satisfy semantic adequacy, transition completeness, invariant preservation, capability completeness, and the observable behaviour contract, has |Capabilities(K*)|=|C_irr|, which combined with the lower bound establishes K* as capability-minimal via the standard lower-bound-plus-construction structure of a minimality proof.

rows.anchor: Packaging theorem. Suppose Capabilities(K_A)=Capabilities(K_B)=C_irr and K_A ==_sem K_B. Then K_A and K_B are two minimal realizations of the same Kernel capability system. They need not have equal operator counts. For example K_A={Interpret,Represent} could be replaced by K_B={SemanticTransform}. I
rows.statement: Proves a packaging theorem: two semantically equivalent implementations K_A, K_B realizing the same irreducible capability set C_irr are both minimal realizations of the same kernel capability system regardless of differing operator counts (e.g. K_A={Interpret,Represent} vs K_B={SemanticTransform}), so a smaller operator count establishes only more compressed implementation packaging, never a smaller epistemic kernel -- explaining why the earlier research concluded operator count is not representation invariant.

rows.anchor: KernelCapability(c) iff c is semantically required and irreducible. DerivedCapability(c) iff c not-in KernelCapability and c=F(C_1,...,C_n) ... This resolves the DetectGap problem. We do not need DetectGap as a primitive if DetectGap = F(Determine,Discriminate,I,Q,EC) ... Capability exists !=> primi
rows.statement: Defines KernelCapability(c) (semantically required and irreducible) versus DerivedCapability(c) (expressible as a composition F of kernel capabilities), formally resolving the DetectGap problem by showing DetectGap=F(Determine,Discriminate,I,Q,EC) under declared semantics, so a capability existing does not imply a primitive kernel operator exists for it.

rows.anchor: Zero is defined over a transformation and preservation observation: Zero_{T,Pi}(S;D) iff Pi(T(D))=Pi(T(E_S(D))). Therefore Zero depends upon D,T,Pi,S. It is not itself an epistemic capability required to construct every kernel state. ... Zero not-in KernelCapability under the current contract. It re
rows.statement: Formally excludes Zero from the primitive kernel: since Zero_{T,Pi}(S;D) is a predicate parameterized by D,T,Pi,S rather than an intrinsic epistemic capability, and the bridge experiments showed Zero neither implies nor is implied by adequacy, Zero not-in KernelCapability under the current contract, remaining instead a transformation-relative eliminability lens.

rows.anchor: For D --T--> R the representation R is a carrier. KnowledgeOS asks whether Q=g.T, or H(Q|R)=0. That establishes representation adequacy. It does not establish that Represent must be an epistemic primitive. ... Representation mechanism != Representation capability != Kernel primitive.
rows.statement: Formally excludes 'Represent' from the primitive kernel merely because every kernel needs some representation: representation adequacy (H(Q|R)=0) does not establish that Represent must itself be an epistemic primitive, since epistemic states may be represented implicitly through state transitions, typed relations, structured records, distributions, graphs, tensors, databases, or symbolic structures -- Representation mechanism != Representation capability != Kernel primitive.

rows.anchor: Select cannot automatically be promoted to the epistemic kernel. Epistemic selection: Select_epi: H_Q -> A_Q. Practical/decision selection: Select_act: A^act -> Action, which belongs downstream: K_t -> Proposal -> Decision -> Authorization -> Action. Therefore Select in Kernel is not established mer
rows.statement: Splits 'Select' into epistemic selection (Select_epi: hypothesis space to admissible hypotheses) and practical/decision selection (Select_act: belonging downstream in the K_t -> Proposal -> Decision -> Authorization -> Action pipeline), concluding Select in Kernel is not established merely because KnowledgeOS ultimately selects actions or hypotheses -- the capability must first be typed, exactly the semantic-granularity instability observed in the earlier reduction experiment.

rows.anchor: Epistemic kernel is responsible only for irreducible epistemic transformations. Representation layer D--T-->R handles representation and reduction. Reasoning regimes provide domain-specific reasoning machinery. Zero Lens examines transformation-relative boundaries. Governance (Authorization) remains
rows.statement: Produces the resulting six-way architecture separating Epistemic Kernel (irreducible epistemic transformations only), Representation Layer (D->R representation/reduction), Reasoning Regimes (domain-specific inference machinery), Zero Lens (transformation-relative boundary analysis), Governance (external authorization), and Execution (external actions) -- Kernel != Representation != Reasoning Engine != Zero != Governance != Execution -- described as a major DDD result: the kernel owns epistemic responsibility, not every mechanism involved in producing or consuming knowledge.

rows.anchor: Theorem -- Relative Semantic Minimality of the KnowledgeOS Kernel. Let E be a fixed KnowledgeOS semantic environment with [10 fixed components including semantic equivalence and a capability set C_irr irreducible under Lemma 1, and a reference implementation K* realizing every capability in C_irr].
rows.statement: Proves the first-pass main theorem (Relative Semantic Minimality of the KnowledgeOS Kernel): given a fixed semantic environment with ten specified fixed components (carrier, inquiry space, contract space, standards, transition semantics, invariant set, observable behaviour, semantic equivalence, an irreducible capability set C_irr, and a reference implementation K* realizing it), K* is minimal under ==_sem, i.e. no kernel satisfying the same contract exists with a strictly smaller capability set.

rows.anchor: Proven conditionally: irreducibility + completeness => minimality. And: different operator packaging !=> different kernel. Experimentally supported: Qualify cannot simply be omitted; DetectGap is derivable; multiple minimal packagings exist; operator counting alone is inadequate ... Not yet universa
rows.statement: Delivers a three-tier honest status ledger for the first-pass proof: proven conditionally (irreducibility plus completeness implies minimality; different operator packaging does not imply a different kernel); experimentally supported (Qualify's non-omissibility, DetectGap's derivability, multiple minimal packagings, inadequacy of raw operator counting); and not yet universally proven (the currently named capability set is not proved to be the unique universal kernel, pending formal closure of semantic equivalence, composition, lifecycle, and invariant preservation).

rows.anchor: We may prove minimal without proving unique implementation. There may exist K_1,...,K_n such that K_i==_sem K_j and each is minimal. Then Kernel capability system is unique while Kernel implementation is not unique. That is exactly the mathematically correct resolution of the two 13-operator minima
rows.statement: Establishes the crucial distinction between minimality and uniqueness: multiple semantically-equivalent implementations K_1,...,K_n can each be minimal, so the Kernel capability system can be unique even while the Kernel implementation is not, which is exactly the mathematically correct resolution of the two 13-operator minima found experimentally.

rows.anchor: I would therefore not freeze 'The KnowledgeOS Kernel consists of 13 operators.' I would freeze the stronger statement: The KnowledgeOS Kernel is the minimal semantically complete set of epistemic capabilities required to preserve the declared KnowledgeOS epistemic contract across admissible represen
rows.statement: Declines to freeze 'the KnowledgeOS Kernel consists of 13 operators', freezing instead the stronger semantic statement that the Kernel is the minimal semantically complete set of epistemic capabilities required to preserve the declared epistemic contract across admissible representations, transitions, and implementations (K_KOS=min_preceq_sem{K:K|=C_KOS}), establishing that kernel minimality is semantic, not syntactic.

rows.anchor: Previously: 'We need to discover the Kernel.' Now: 'We have a formal criterion under which Kernel minimality can be proved.' The remaining work is no longer conceptual exploration. It is proof closure: Candidate capabilities -> formal witnesses -> semantic equivalence -> completeness -> minimality.
rows.statement: Marks a phase shift in the research status from 'we need to discover the Kernel' to 'we have a formal criterion under which Kernel minimality can be proved', reframing the remaining work as proof closure (candidate capabilities -> formal witnesses -> semantic equivalence -> completeness -> minimality) rather than conceptual exploration.

rows.anchor: Mathematically: the minimality argument above is valid as a relative theorem, provided its semantic contract and irreducibility witnesses are formally instantiated. Statistically: existing experiments provide evidence for the irreducibility hypotheses, but empirical frequency cannot substitute for t
rows.statement: Delivers a four-part senior-level verdict on pass 1 (mathematically valid as a relative theorem pending formal instantiation; statistically supported by experiments that cannot substitute for the theorem's universal quantifiers; DDD-correct ownership boundary established; epistemically premature to promote candidate capability names to universal primitives), concluding Kernel Minimality is formally characterized and conditionally proved but the unique final Kernel is not yet universally proven -- explicitly framing that distinction as what makes the proof rigorous rather than a weakness.

rows.anchor: we should not yet ratify the phrase 'minimality proof' without qualification. The correct status is: Conditional Minimality Theorem Schema until [ten components: admissible state space, inquiry space, contract/context space, transition relation, observable space, observational equality, history sema
rows.statement: A critical second-pass review demotes the pass-1 result from 'minimality proof' to 'Conditional Minimality Theorem Schema', since the semantic-equivalence definition's Obs function remains a placeholder until ten components are formally specified (admissible state space, inquiry space, contract/context space, transition relation, observable space, observational equality, history semantics, invariant set, attribution semantics, allowed environment interactions).

rows.anchor: A capability is not necessarily irreducible simply because one implementation of the remaining capabilities fails to reproduce it. To prove genuine irreducibility, we need something closer to: for all K' [Capabilities(K') subseteq C\{c} => K' not-equiv_sem K]. The witness must rule out every admissi
rows.statement: Identifies the decisive flaw in the pass-1 irreducibility lemma: it only ruled out one tested composition of the remaining capabilities, not every admissible alternative realization; genuine irreducibility requires the universal statement 'for all K' with Capabilities(K') subseteq C\{c}, K' is not semantically equivalent to K', i.e. the witness must rule out every admissible alternative realization, not merely the one tested.

rows.anchor: the old Kernel experiment has a precise role. They become lower-bound evidence. ... DetectGap was shown to be derivable across the tested variants. Therefore ... DetectGap !=> primitive. Capability exists != Capability is primitive != Capability is universally irreducible.
rows.statement: Reassigns the old 13-operator kernel experiments the precise role of lower-bound evidence (not proof), sharpening the three-way distinction: capability exists != capability is primitive != capability is universally irreducible, with DetectGap's demonstrated derivability across tested variants as the concrete instance where existence does not imply primitiveness.

rows.anchor: The 13/14 capability list should therefore remain provisional. ... these are a candidate capability universe, not 13 primitives. I would keep it exactly at that status. Do not freeze this list yet.
rows.statement: Insists the 13-item candidate capability list remain explicitly provisional (a candidate capability universe, never 13 confirmed primitives) and must not be frozen yet.

rows.anchor: The factivity work is important because it prevents a hidden assumption: Knowledge(p) => Truth(p) from being silently implemented by the Kernel. ... the Kernel may produce an epistemic attribution without manufacturing truth. ... The minimality theory should retain it because otherwise 'Validate' ca
rows.statement: Argues the factivity boundary (E_t--Gamma-->A_t kept separate from truth verification) must remain part of the minimality theory since without it, a hidden Knowledge(p)=>Truth(p) assumption could be silently implemented by the Kernel and 'Validate' could secretly become 'make true.'

rows.anchor: Define the KnowledgeOS semantic contract: C_K = (X,Q,C,E,H,S,I,O,Theta) ... A Kernel is then an implementation: K=(X_K, delta_K, Cap_K, Inv_K, Obs_K). This is substantially better than defining the Kernel as a tuple of named operators.
rows.statement: Redefines the KnowledgeOS semantic contract as a nine-tuple C_K=(X,Q,C,E,H,S,I,O,Theta) (epistemic states, inquiries, contexts, admissible evidence, hypothesis spaces, standards, invariants, observable outcomes, allowed transition semantics), with a Kernel implementation K=(X_K,delta_K,Cap_K,Inv_K,Obs_K) -- explicitly judged substantially better than defining the Kernel as a tuple of named operators.

rows.anchor: Tr_K(h) = (o_0,...,o_n) with o_t=(K_t,Delta_t,Det_t,Rev_t,Attr_t,Inv_t,Hist_t). K1 ==_sem K2 iff forall h in H_adm, Tr_K1(h)=Tr_K2(h). ... K_A not-cong_syntactic K_B while K_A ==_sem K_B. That means there is potentially one semantic Kernel with multiple implementations.
rows.statement: Repairs the semantic-equivalence definition by replacing pointwise Obs equality with trace equivalence over admissible input histories: Tr_K(h)=(o_0,...,o_n) with each o_t a seven-component observable (K_t,Delta_t,Det_t,Rev_t,Attr_t,Inv_t,Hist_t), and K1 ==_sem K2 iff Tr_K1(h)=Tr_K2(h) for every admissible history h, resolving the two-13-operator puzzle since K_A can be syntactically non-isomorphic to K_B while trace-equivalent, i.e. one semantic Kernel can have multiple implementations.

rows.anchor: Irred(c|C) iff forall K' [Capabilities(K') subseteq C\{c} => K' not-equiv_sem K_C]. ... There is no admissible implementation using the remaining capabilities that is semantically equivalent. That is a genuine universal statement.
rows.statement: Fixes the irreducibility definition into a genuine universal statement Irred(c|C) iff for all K' with Capabilities(K') subseteq C\{c}, K' is not semantically (trace-)equivalent to K_C -- there is no admissible implementation using only the remaining capabilities that is semantically equivalent -- correcting pass 1's weaker single-witness formulation.

rows.anchor: Let W_c subseteq H_adm be a set of admissible histories. We require: forall K' [Capabilities(K') subseteq C\{c} => exists h in W_c: Tr_K'(h) != Tr_K(h)]. Then c is irreducible. ... capability -> irreducibility witness family -> alternative implementation elimination -> universal irreducibility.
rows.statement: Constructs a practical irreducibility-witness family W_c (a set of admissible histories) such that every implementation restricted to the remaining capabilities fails to match some trace in W_c, giving a concrete four-step pipeline (capability -> irreducibility witness family -> alternative implementation elimination -> universal irreducibility) approximated empirically by the existing kernel experiments.

rows.anchor: Complete(K,C_K) iff forall h in H_adm, K |= C_K meaning it satisfies [9 semantics: epistemic state, inquiry, evidence handling, revision, determination, required invariants, attribution boundary, lifecycle semantics, observable contract]. ... If Complete(K*,C_K) and Capabilities(K*)=C*, we have the
rows.statement: Defines Complete(K,C_K) as K satisfying nine required semantics (epistemic state, inquiry, evidence handling, revision, determination, required invariants, attribution boundary, lifecycle, observable contract) across every admissible history, giving the upper bound once a reference capability set C* is shown Complete via some K*.

rows.anchor: Theorem -- KnowledgeOS Relative Semantic Kernel Minimality. Let K* be complete satisfying C_K. Assume A1 fixed semantic contract, A2 fixed observable semantics Tr_K, A3 semantic equivalence is trace equivalence, A4 completeness of K*, A5 irreducibility of every c in C*. Then: not-exists K' [Capabili
rows.statement: Proves the fully rigorous final theorem (KnowledgeOS Relative Semantic Kernel Minimality): under five explicit assumptions (A1 fixed semantic contract, A2 fixed trace-based observable semantics, A3 semantic equivalence as trace equivalence, A4 completeness of K*, A5 irreducibility of every capability in Capabilities(K*)), no kernel K' with a strictly smaller capability set can be both complete and semantically equivalent to K*, proved by contradiction using the now-universal irreducibility definition -- explicitly marked as now a proper mathematical theorem, unlike the pass-1 schema.

rows.anchor: It does not claim |K*|=globally smallest number of functions. Nor smallest number of classes. Nor K* is the only implementation. Instead: K* is minimal in semantic capability space. There may be K_1 != K_2 internally, with K_1 ==_sem K_2 and both minimal. That is not a defect. It is the mathematical
rows.statement: Clarifies what the final theorem does not claim -- not a globally smallest function or class count, not a unique implementation -- only minimality in semantic capability space, with internally distinct but trace-equivalent implementations both being minimal, explicitly framed as the mathematically correct result rather than a defect.

rows.anchor: Old interpretation: There are two minimal Kernels of size 13. Correct interpretation: The tested search space contained two semantically distinct operator packagings of equal cardinality that satisfied the tested capability requirements. Those may actually represent K_A ==_sem K_B. If so: two implem
rows.statement: Formally reinterprets the earlier discovery of two minimal 13-operator kernel configurations: rather than 'two minimal Kernels of size 13', the correct reading is that the search space contained two operator packagings of equal cardinality, which if trace-equivalent are the same semantic kernel realized twice -- two implementations do not equal two Kernels.

rows.anchor: Class(c) in {Primitive, Derived, Representation, Domain, Governance, Execution, Open}. DetectGap -> Derived has already received strong experimental support. Select remains semantically ambiguous because Select_epi != Select_act. The latter belongs downstream to decision/action.
rows.statement: Requires classifying every candidate capability into one of seven classes (Primitive, Derived, Representation, Domain, Governance, Execution, Open), with DetectGap already strongly supported as Derived and Select remaining ambiguous pending resolution of the Select_epi versus Select_act split, the latter belonging downstream to decision/action.

rows.anchor: The final DDD boundary: Kernel = irreducible epistemic capabilities. Representation = encode/reduce while preserving inquiry contract. Reasoning Regime = statistical/logical/causal/etc. inference. Zero Lens = transformation-relative eliminability/boundary analysis. Governance = authorization and ins
rows.statement: Finalizes the six-way DDD responsibility table -- Kernel (irreducible epistemic capabilities), Representation (encode/reduce while preserving the inquiry contract), Reasoning Regime (statistical/logical/causal inference), Zero Lens (transformation-relative eliminability/boundary analysis), Governance (authorization and institutional constraints), Execution (actions in the external world) -- explicitly judged probably the most important DDD outcome of the whole research programme.

rows.anchor: Research closure: Broad foundational discovery = CLOSED. Mathematical characterization: Kernel minimality criterion = DEFINED. Universal instantiated Kernel: FINAL KERNEL = NOT YET PROVEN.
rows.statement: States the three decisive final closure statements: broad foundational discovery is CLOSED, the Kernel minimality criterion is now formally DEFINED, but the universal instantiated FINAL KERNEL is NOT YET PROVEN.

rows.anchor: No more random operator discovery, new philosophical analogies, new Vedic algebra, new Zero algebra, new compression metaphors, arbitrary operator counting. Instead: FIX CONTRACT -> FIX CARRIER -> FIX TRACE/OBSERVABLES -> DEFINE SEMANTIC EQUIVALENCE -> TYPE CAPABILITIES -> PROVE DERIVABILITY -> CONS
rows.statement: Freezes the research direction, explicitly ruling out further random operator discovery, new philosophical analogies, new Vedic or Zero algebras, compression metaphors, and arbitrary operator counting, replacing them with a closed twelve-step mathematical proof-construction pipeline from fixing the contract and carrier through defining semantic equivalence, typing capabilities, proving derivability, constructing irreducibility witnesses, proving completeness, establishing lower and upper bounds, minimality, and finally checking uniqueness -- reframing the remaining work as a closed proof problem rather than an open discovery problem.

rows.anchor: The final theorem is: Complete(K*,C_K) and forall c in Capabilities(K*), Irred(c) and ==_sem fixed => K* is a semantically minimal KnowledgeOS Kernel. That is the kernel minimality proof.
rows.statement: States the compact final theorem: Complete(K*,C_K) together with irreducibility of every capability in Capabilities(K*) and a fixed trace-based semantic equivalence together imply K* is a semantically minimal KnowledgeOS Kernel -- declared to be the kernel minimality proof in its final, corrected form.

rows.anchor: Lemma 1: Universal Capability Irreducibility Witness. A capability c* is universally irreducible ... iff there exists a state-inquiry witness pair (x_w,q_w) and an invariant i such that [transition via c* preserves i and yields valid observation; every composite transition F from the remaining capab
rows.statement: Presents a parallel formalization of capability irreducibility (Lemma 1: Universal Capability Irreducibility Witness) requiring a witness state-inquiry pair (x_w,q_w) and invariant i such that the capability's transition preserves i and yields a valid observation while every composite transition built purely from the remaining capabilities either produces a different observation or violates the invariant, proved by contradiction against the assumption of derivability.

rows.anchor: Theorem 1: Absolute Minimality of the Irreducible Capability Basis (C_irr). Let C_irr={c_1,...,c_m} where every element satisfies Lemma 1. Let K* be a reference implementation whose capability set is precisely C_irr. Then K* is semantically minimal ... Proof of Theorem 1: [contradiction via witness]
rows.statement: Proves a parallel Theorem 1 (Absolute Minimality of the Irreducible Capability Basis): given a capability set C_irr where every element satisfies the witness-based irreducibility Lemma 1, a reference implementation K* realizing exactly C_irr is semantically minimal, since no proper subset can be semantically complete under the fixed contract.

rows.anchor: FactiveCheck(A_t,T) = 1 if A_t(p)=Asserted and T(p)=True, 0 otherwise. The kernel does not manufacture T(p); it manages E_t --Gamma--> A_t. This prevents truth verification from corrupting kernel minimality.
rows.statement: Reformalizes the factivity boundary as an explicit external FactiveCheck(A_t,T) predicate (evaluating to 1 only if the kernel's assertion A_t(p) matches the external truth T(p)), keeping the kernel's own operation confined to managing the attribution E_t--Gamma-->A_t without manufacturing T(p) itself, to prevent truth verification from corrupting kernel minimality.

rows.anchor: Select_epi: H_Q x S -> H_Q' (Internal to Kernel). Select_act: A^act x Policy -> Action (External to Kernel). Only Select_epi is a candidate for K_epi. Select_act belongs downstream in execution and governance. ... Zero_{T,Pi} ... is a higher-order evaluation operator over kernel states, not an eleme
rows.statement: Restates the Select_epi/Select_act typing split (only Select_epi is a kernel candidate; Select_act belongs to downstream execution/governance) and the Zero exclusion (Zero_{T,Pi} is a higher-order evaluation operator over kernel states dependent on D,T,Pi,S, hence not an elementary capability, so Zero is not in C_irr).

rows.anchor: class EpistemicKernel: def run(self, cap_name, state, **kwargs) ... def observe_kernel_behaviour(kernel, scenario_steps, initial_state) -> (StateDigest, InvariantPreserved). class MinimalityVerificationSuite: def test_irreducibility_witness(...) [ablation: compares reference digest vs reduced-capabi
rows.statement: Provides an executable Python verification testbed for the kernel-minimality theory: EpistemicState with a deterministic SHA-256 digest, a Capability interface with Interpret/Qualify/Hypothesize implementations and a DerivedDetectGap capability computed from qualifier thresholds, an EpistemicKernel container, an observe_kernel_behaviour function returning (state digest, invariant-preserved flag) over a scenario, and a MinimalityVerificationSuite offering test_irreducibility_witness (ablation testing: does removing a named capability change the observed digest or invariant status) and test_reference_relative_encoding (computing a delta between base and target states, reconstructing, and checking lossless recovery plus compression ratio) -- an actual runnable operationalization of the formal minimality/irreducibility and reference-relative-encoding definitions.

rows.anchor: KNOWLEDGEOS RESEARCH REGISTER: KR-KERNEL-MINIMALITY-2026-09 (RATIFIED) ... AUTHORITY: KnowledgeOS Core Epistemic Framework Committee ... STATUS: [RATIFIED CONDITIONAL THEOREM SCHEMA]
rows.statement: Self-declares KR-KERNEL-MINIMALITY-2026-09 'RATIFIED' by a named 'KnowledgeOS Core Epistemic Framework Committee' -- a governance claim that a subsequent review in this same document flags as unauthorized (no such committee or ratification act is shown to actually exist) and retracts, per the corpus's established pattern of self-declared ratification status being unreliable until independently verified against an actual governance record.

lineage_claims.target: the RATIFIED claim in this same file
lineage_claims.quote: Unless that committee and ratification act actually exist in your governance system, this must not appear as a factual ratification.

rows.anchor: Unless that committee and ratification act actually exist in your governance system, this must not appear as a factual ratification. Given our standing provenance discipline, we cannot manufacture governance authority. It should instead say: STATUS: PROPOSED RESEARCH REGISTER ENTRY ... STATUS OF RAT
rows.statement: Catches and corrects the unauthorized 'RATIFIED' governance claim in the same document, insisting that without an actually-existing committee and ratification act, the entry must not appear as a factual ratification, and must instead read 'PROPOSED RESEARCH REGISTER ENTRY' with ratification status 'NOT RATIFIED' -- explicitly calling this a provenance error of exactly the kind KnowledgeOS is supposed to prevent.

rows.anchor: competing Kernel may realize the same semantic capability through a different decomposition. C*={A,B,C} might be implemented by K1={A,B,C} while another implementation has K2={X,Y} where X,Y jointly realize exactly the same semantic powers. Then Capabilities(K2) not-subseteq C* syntactically, even t
rows.statement: Identifies a gap in the subset-based minimality theorem: a competing kernel K2={X,Y} might realize exactly the same semantic capabilities as K1={A,B,C} through an entirely different decomposition, so Capabilities(K2) is not even a syntactic subset of C* despite K1==_sem K2 -- requiring the theorem to quantify over admissible implementations and realization mappings rather than mere subsets of one named capability list.

rows.anchor: K*|=C_K and forall K in K_adm, K==_sem K* => C_irr preceq_cap K. Then K* realizing exactly C_irr gives the upper bound. This handles alternative implementation decompositions correctly.

rows.statement: States the clean target definition of semantic minimality: K* in MinKer(C) iff K* satisfies the contract and no strictly capability-smaller admissible K' also satisfies it, i.e. K* is a minimal element of the contract-satisfying set under preceq_cap -- explicitly not a minimum operator count.

rows.statement: Commissions KR-CONTR-2026-09: mission is to determine whether contradiction can be represented without collapsing into uncertainty/absence/insufficient-evidence/theory-incompleteness/unobservability/non-assessment, whether the current 3-valued domain is expressive enough, what the minimum evaluation domain must contain, whether a 4th value C is actually necessary, and whether contradiction has kernel implications.

rows.statement: Requires the experiment to preserve a seven-layer non-collapse chain (World≠Observation≠Evidence≠Interpretation≠EpistemicState≠Evaluation≠KnowledgeAttribution) and forbids giving the simulated agent access to hidden ground truth: Contr(p,Kt) must not mean 'the world makes both p and not-p true' but that the epistemic representation simultaneously contains incompatible commitments about p.

rows.statement: Specifies the four candidate representations to test fairly: A) extend {T,F,U} to {T,F,U,C}, testing whether C is primitive/derivable/needs provenance or polarity/can coexist with U; B) keep Sat in {T,F,U} and represent Contr(p,K) as an independent relation outside Sat; C) exclusive-by-construction (bot ≡ not-p∈K ∧ p∉K), explicitly flagged as expected-vulnerable to silently converting contradictory into false/absent/invalid; D) a structured EVal=(value,reason,provenance,evidence,context,time,polarity) tuple whose exact fields must be discovered by reduction.

rows.anchor:
$$

\quad
x\neq y
\Rightarrow
R(x)\neq R(y).
$$
rows.statement: Formalizes representation adequacy for this experiment: a candidate representation R:S->D is adequate iff for every required distinction pair (x,y) in R_req, x≠y implies R(x)≠R(y); a structured representation may satisfy this even when two conditions share the same primary 'value' field, so uniqueness of the primary value is not required.

rows.anchor: ### Case 1 — Unknown ... ### Case 15 — Model conflict
rows.statement: Specifies a 15-case deterministic adversarial suite: unknown, absent, not-assessed, insufficient evidence, underdetermined, unobservable, direct contradiction, conflicting sources, conflicting observations, unequal-confidence contradiction, retraction, supersession, different contexts, different times, and model conflict -- each with an expected semantic condition and an instruction not to prejudge borderline cases (e.g. source conflict vs epistemic contradiction, retraction should not automatically create contradiction).

rows.statement: Poses the Zero-interaction question as genuinely open: does contradiction imply Zero, does it not, or does contradiction require its own separate Zero classification -- to be decided by evidence, not assumed.

Therefore investigate whether... `ZeroLens(K_t)` can expose `contradiction` without becoming `Contradiction = Zero`
rows.statement: Requires testing whether ZeroLens can expose contradiction without collapsing into identifying contradiction with Zero itself; a contradiction may be fully represented (hence not a representational absence) while still creating an unresolved requirement -- these are different questions that must not be conflated.

rows.statement: Permits investigating Belnap four-valued semantics, paraconsistent semantics, Kleene semantics, Priest-style approaches and bilattice structures, but only as tagged [EXT] research references never automatically imported; the governing question is what KnowledgeOS empirically/formally requires, not which existing logic to adopt -- any useful external logic must have its mapping explicitly demonstrated.

rows.statement: Specifies the minimality procedure: for a structured representation R=(value,reason,provenance,evidence,context,time,status), test removing each field individually (R_-f); if removal collapses a required distinction, f is empirically necessary for the tested representation (not universally necessary) -- an experimental minimality result only.

rows.anchor: ### Positive capability test ... ### Negative separation test ... ### Completeness test ... ### Minimality test
rows.statement: Warns against vacuous success: a candidate must not pass merely because all contradictory cases collapse to U (if the oracle requires contradiction stay distinct) nor because everything is classified C (which preserves contradiction while destroying all other distinctions); requires four separate tests -- positive capability, negative separation, completeness, and minimality.

rows.statement: Requires distinguishing Representation, Responsibility, Evaluation, and Governance: representing contradiction does not imply the kernel must resolve it; detecting contradiction does not imply resolving it; resolving contradiction does not imply determining truth.

rows.anchor:
> Does contradiction introduce a genuinely irreducible kernel capability?

Test whether contradiction handling can be expressed through existing candidate powers such as: Observe, Interpret, Represent, Relate, Discriminate, Hypothesize, DetectGap, Challenge, Validate, Revise, Determine, Select, Qualify
rows.statement: Poses the kernel-irreducibility question: must contradiction be added to the kernel as a new operator, or can it be derived through existing candidate powers (Observe/Interpret/Represent/Relate/Discriminate/Hypothesize/DetectGap/Challenge/Validate/Revise/Determine/Select/Qualify)? Explicitly notes the outcome may be 'contradiction is a semantic state' rather than 'a kernel operator', and that this distinction is mandatory.

rows.anchor: ### NEG-1 ... A fourth value `C` cannot distinguish important subtypes of contradiction. ... ### NEG-8 ... A supposedly minimal representation loses provenance or temporal distinctions.
rows.statement: Pre-registers eight candidate negative results to actively search for (NEG-1..8): a fourth value C cannot distinguish contradiction subtypes; structured evaluation still collapses required distinctions; contradiction is context-dependent and cannot be represented without context; contradiction is temporal and cannot be represented statically; source conflict is not epistemic contradiction; contradiction cannot be reduced to Sat; Zero cannot be determined from contradiction alone; a supposedly minimal representation loses provenance or temporal distinctions.

$$ ... ### Candidate I10 ... Historical contradiction and current contradiction may differ.
rows.statement: Pre-registers ten candidate invariants to test rather than assume (I1-I10): Contr is not equivalent to Unknown/Absent/NotAssessed/InsufficientEvidence/Unobservable/TruthFailure/Zero (I7 conditional on no formal mapping being established); DetectContradiction ≠ ResolveContradiction (I8); ResolveContradiction ≠ DetermineTruth (I9); historical and current contradiction may differ (I10).

rows.statement: Poses a candidate separation for testing: evidence conflict (E1 entails p, E2 entails not-p) does not automatically create contradictory epistemic commitments at the claim level -- EvidenceConflict may be distinct from ClaimContradiction, and likewise ModelConflict (M1 entails p, M2 entails not-p) may be a distinct concept from either.

rows.statement: Mandates a six-way decision-gate verdict (A: three-valued domain sufficient, B: fourth value required, C: structured evaluation required, D: more than four values required, E: contradiction represented outside Sat, F: question remains underdetermined -- or a defined new status if none fits) as the experiment's required output.

rows.statement: Mandates a five-way kernel verdict (K0-K4) as required output, with K3 requiring a genuine irreducibility argument since 'importance is not irreducibility'.

States the experiment's final governing principle in three boxed statements: represent what evidence requires, not what theory wishes; contradiction must not be collapsed into uncertainty merely for lack of a separate value; contradiction must not be promoted to a primitive merely because it feels intuitively important -- the choice between these two errors must be made by constructive separation, adversarial witnesses, minimality analysis and explicit DDD semantics.

rows.anchor: **The prompt instructions are APPROVED.** This is the most rigorously constructed experiment prompt in the entire KnowledgeOS programme.
rows.statement: HPA Supervisory review approves the KR-CONTR-2026-09 prompt as ready for execution, calling it the most rigorously constructed experiment prompt in the programme, and independently verifies it against the three prior register corrections (Factivity/Contr independence, no predetermined fourth-value assumption, discover-the-minimum-domain framing), confirming the prompt satisfies all three.

Identifies the current research bottleneck as Contradiction->Evaluation->Representation->Zero and recommends reading non-classical logic (Priest, Belnap/Dunn) with the specific purpose of understanding which distinctions different logical systems preserve or collapse -- not to find 'the KnowledgeOS logic'.

True(p)\land True(\neg p).

rows.statement: Warns against adopting Priest's dialetheist conclusion (some contradictions are true) as a KnowledgeOS assumption: p,¬p∈E_t does not imply True(p)∧True(¬p) -- KnowledgeOS's contradiction problem is epistemic inconsistency, not ontological/semantic contradiction, a distinction it calls extremely important.

rows.anchor: we should not decide the Contr experiment before reading this material. The next experiment should remain adversarial; the books provide candidate mathematical structures against which the experiment can test KnowledgeOS, not answers that KnowledgeOS must adopt.
rows.statement: Constrains how the recommended literature should be used: the Contr experiment must remain adversarial and must not be decided by reading first -- the books supply candidate mathematical structures to test KnowledgeOS against, never answers to adopt.

rows.statement: Extracts Priest's paraconsistency/non-explosion principle (inconsistency need not entail arbitrary conclusions, illustrated via inconsistent scientific theories and legislation) as a candidate for Contr: contradiction should produce a localized effect, not global inferential collapse -- tagged [PROP], explicitly not yet a kernel invariant.

rows.statement: Extracts Priest's gap/glut distinction (neither-true-nor-false vs both-true-and-false, driving K3/L3 vs LP/RM3 three-valued systems) as formal justification for the Zero Lens's discipline of not collapsing Unknown/Absent/NotAssessed/Unresolved/Contradiction/Unobservable/Underdetermined into one value.

where ... $$

$$

rows.statement: Extracts FDE's core representation (a proposition maps to independent support-for-A and support-for-not-A) as a candidate two-channel evaluation Eval(p)=(S+(p),S-(p)) with four structural states (supported/opposed/conflicting/unsupported); explicitly tagged as not-yet-theory, requiring testing against the nine-state/14-boundary Zero experiments: [EXT] FDE -> [PROP] two-channel representation -> [EXP] must be tested.

This strongly confirms something we already discovered experimentally: **evaluation status and boundary reason must not be collapsed.**
rows.statement: Warns that FDE's four truth-value states are NOT the same dimension as KnowledgeOS's Zero boundary-reason categories: two situations with identical FDE support-values (0,0) can have entirely different KnowledgeOS reasons (no assessment vs fundamental unobservability) -- FDE_status(P)≠ZeroBoundary(P), reinforcing that evaluation status and boundary reason must not be collapsed, consistent with the prior KR-ZERO finding that facet keys alone cannot distinguish some conditions.

and

The same object can occur in both.
rows.statement: Extracts Priest's relational-FDE extension/anti-extension machinery (a predicate's extension records positive support, anti-extension records negative support, the same object can occur in both) as a candidate ClaimStanding structure Standing(p)=(E+(p),E-(p)) with provenance attached to each side, supporting positive-evidence/negative-evidence/conflict/absence without forcing immediate resolution.

but not:

$$
rows.statement: Proposes, from Priest's example of conflicting legal rules not invalidating the whole legal system, a candidate invariant that contradiction implies local conflict but not global invalidity -- Rule A->X, Rule B->¬X should produce Conflict(X), not KnowledgeSpace=invalid; tagged [PROP], to be tested.

rows.anchor: Instead ask: **What distinctions must the representation preserve?** For one proposition p, test at least: positive evidence, negative evidence, conflict, no assessment... then add unobservable, underdetermined, not assessed, temporally superseded, scope-excluded
rows.statement: Recommends the Contr experiment reject the framing 'how many states do we need' (repeating the earlier N_eff-style mistake) in favor of 'what distinctions must the representation preserve', proposing a concrete test table crossing p/¬p support levels with unobservable/underdetermined/not-assessed/superseded/scope-excluded conditions, checked for orthogonal representability without corrupting the four-valued core.

Test against: four-valued FDE representation, current 3-valued model, structured (value,reason,provenance), four-way boundary model, candidate fourth-value model.
rows.statement: Proposes updating the research interpretation (not Theory v1.2) of TODO Group B: candidate Contr(p)=Support+(p)∧Support-(p), to be tested against five representations (FDE, current 3-valued, structured value/reason/provenance, four-way boundary, candidate fourth value) -- this is the direct precursor formulation to the Contr(p,K)=Pos∧Neg definition later formalized in the KR-CONTR-2026-09 protocol (S2484).

Not established... ### ❌ "FDE is the KnowledgeOS kernel."

Absolutely not... ### ❌ "Relevant logic proves Evidence relevance."

No
rows.statement: Explicitly rejects eleven tempting overclaims from the Priest extraction: KnowledgeOS should use FDE; KnowledgeOS has exactly four epistemic states; contradiction is true; KnowledgeOS is paraconsistent; FDE is the KnowledgeOS kernel; Zero equals the fourth FDE value; Unknown equals neither-true-nor-false; Contradiction equals both-true-and-false; possible worlds equal Knowledge Space; relevant logic proves evidence relevance; many-valued logic gives the correct epistemic ontology.

rows.statement: Proposes the strongest research candidate architecture extracted from the book: an evaluation-layer pipeline Evidence->Assessment->Standing->Determination->Attribution, with Standing(p)=(S+(p),S-(p)) as an FDE-inspired core kept separate from Boundary(p)=(Facet,Condition,Context,Provenance) recording why the state is incomplete, and Determination(Q)⊆H_Q recording remaining alternatives -- explicitly not Theory v1.3.

\times

where the first factor could potentially be FDE-like
rows.statement: Reformulates the research question from 'how many Zero states' to 'what independent semantic dimensions are required to represent support/opposition/incompleteness/contradiction without collapsing distinct non-determination reasons', proposing a candidate factorization EpistemicEvaluation = Truth/Falsity-Support × Boundary-Condition × Context × Provenance, with minimality/sufficiency/correctness left explicitly open.

rows.anchor:
## `KR-CONTR-FDE-2026-09`

### Question

> Can an FDE-inspired two-channel semantic representation preserve the distinctions required by KnowledgeOS Contr and Zero without collapsing boundary reasons?
rows.statement: Recommends a specific next experiment KR-CONTR-FDE-2026-09 comparing four models (Classical {T,F}, K3 {T,F,U}, FDE {T,F,B,N}, Structured (S+,S-,Reason,Provenance,Context)) against fourteen test scenarios, measuring which distinctions each preserves and which distinct KnowledgeOS situations collapse to the same representation -- framed as a direct continuation of KR-ZERO and FR-001.

States the book's greatest contribution as the principle 'do not force epistemic reality into a single classical truth axis', paired with the closing methodological rule 'a mathematically defined semantics still has to earn its meaning' -- final disposition: Theory v1.2 unchanged, Contr remains next experiment, FDE becomes a major external candidate for that experiment, not the answer.

rows.anchor: | **question** | direct an experiment | assert an answer | | **lens** | make a distinction visible | become the thing it makes visible | | **corroboration** | agree, from outside, with something already derived | serve as the evidence for it |
rows.statement: Establishes the study's binding methodological constraint (from the v1.2 constitutional ban on Gita-concept-to-architecture derivation): the study may produce only questions (direct an experiment, never assert an answer), lenses (make a distinction visible, never become the thing it makes visible), or corroborations (agree from outside with something already derived, never serve as evidence for it); a fourth kind, entity, is never produced and any apparent entity is recorded as a refusal.

rows.anchor: Arjuna's state at 1.28–47 is: **not uncertainty**...**not absence**...**not insufficient evidence**...**not unobservability**...**not non-assessment**
rows.statement: Analyzes Arjuna's viṣāda (Gita 1.28-47) as independently arriving, roughly 2000 years earlier, at exactly the KR-CONTR-2026-09 protocol's required-distinction list: his state is not uncertainty, not absence, not insufficient evidence, not unobservability, and not non-assessment -- corroboration of the distinctions, not evidence for any representation of them.

rows.anchor: > **Lens L-1 — "informed paralysis".** A state may be **complete in evidence and still non-actionable.** Non-actionability is therefore **not** a deficit of evidence and cannot be repaired by acquiring more.
rows.statement: Names Lens L-1, 'informed paralysis': a state can be complete in evidence yet non-actionable (two active, endorsed, mutually incompatible commitments, neither retracted nor superseded, producing not a wrong answer but no answer) -- non-actionability is not an evidence deficit and cannot be repaired by more evidence.

rows.anchor: > **Corroboration C-1** of `KR-CONTR-2026-09` §12: **`EvidenceConflict ≠ ClaimContradiction ≠ ModelConflict`.**
rows.statement: Corroboration C-1: Arjuna diagnoses his own confusion as located specifically in dharma (the normative model), not perception or evidence -- corroborating KR-CONTR-2026-09 §12's EvidenceConflict≠ClaimContradiction≠ModelConflict separation from an independent source, sustained for eighteen chapters of the text.

rows.anchor: > **Corroboration C-2** — for the programme's open item **`⪰`**. ... this locus is corroboration for `⪰` **only**. It says nothing about `N_eff`, and must not be recruited for it.
rows.statement: Corroboration C-2: Arjuna's 'nor do we know which of the two is the weightier' (2.6) is an absent comparative ordering, not a factual doubt -- corroborating that ⪰ is the harder, independent open problem; explicitly restricted to corroborating ⪰ only, forbidden from being recruited to support N_eff given the programme's established N_eff/⪰ independence ruling.

rows.anchor: > **Lens L-2 — "the frame, not the value".**... **This is a lens on the fourth-value question, and it must not be read as an answer to it.**
rows.statement: Names Lens L-2, 'the frame, not the value': the Gita's prescription for a dvandva (pair of opposites) is dvandva-atita, changing the frame in which the pair was posed, rather than picking a side, averaging, or adding a third term -- a lens on the fourth-value question, explicitly stating that KR-CONTR-2026-09's finding that the obstruction is not the number of values was settled by proof, not by this reading, and reversing that priority would itself be the banned derivation.

rows.anchor: > **Corroboration C-3:** **doubt ≠ contradiction**, from an independent tradition... This study therefore does NOT introduce a second `saṃśaya` candidate.** It **extends the existing one**
rows.statement: Corroboration C-3: the Gita treats saṃśaya (doubt, cut by instruction) and viṣāda (contradiction/paralysis, not removed by instruction alone) as two distinct pathologies with two distinct remedies -- corroborating Contr≠Unknown. Per ES-005.4 discipline, this explicitly extends (rather than duplicates) the corpus's existing samsaya-structured-doubt-state candidate (from a prior Nyaya extraction) with a new contrast the Nyaya source lacked: samsaya initiates inquiry, visada halts it -- same family, opposite dynamics.

rows.anchor: > **Lens L-3 — "proportion, not selection".** A representation may need to say **how much of each** rather than **which one**.
rows.statement: Names Lens L-3, 'proportion, not selection': the three guṇas (sattva/rajas/tamas) coexist in every state, differing in proportion rather than one obtaining exclusively -- a lens on KR-CONTR-2026-09 §11's finding that contradiction has internal structure (10 subtypes under a structured representation vs 2 under a flat one), explicitly not concluding KnowledgeOS should adopt a three-component proportion vector.

rows.anchor: | **a definition of `Contr`** | the text describes a contradiction; it never formalises the relation | | **the frame qualifier `φ`** |... | **a value domain** |... | **an ordering `⪰`** | 2.6 states its **absence** as the problem. **Naming a problem is not solving it** |
rows.statement: States explicitly what the Gita does not supply: no definition of Contr, no content for the frame qualifier φ (dvandva-atita says change frame but not which features must agree), no bearing on cardinality of a value domain, no ordering ⪰ (2.6 only names its absence as the problem), and no kernel capability.

rows.anchor: > **Four of ten findings get nothing from the text, and the two most technically load-bearing are among them.** That is the expected shape of an honest corroboration study.
rows.statement: Tabulates a ten-row corroboration map against KR-CONTR-2026-09 findings, explicitly noting four rows (including 'minimum structure is a pair containing reason' and 'χ ranges 3-21', the two most technically load-bearing) get no textual support at all -- offered as evidence the study is reading the text honestly rather than reading itself into it.

rows.anchor: | **G-1** | **informed paralysis**... | **G-6** | **exhaust evidence, then decide** | **corroboration** | `[EXT]` | 18.63 | **nothing — it is already derived internally.**
rows.statement: Registers six typed candidates (G-1 informed paralysis as lens [PROP]; G-2 whether reason needs a layer field, as an open question; G-3 the samsaya/visada extension as lens [PROP] requiring a second independent adopter per ES-006.1; G-4 frame-change-as-response as lens [PROP]; G-5 proportion-vs-selection as open lens; G-6 exhaust-then-decide as [EXT] corroboration needing no promotion since already derived internally) and explicitly refuses five would-be entities (dharma, guna, ksetra/ksetrajna, dvandva-atita-as-operator, visada-as-state-value) as violations of the constitutional ban.

rows.anchor:
> ## **The Gītā supplies NO kernel candidate. Not one.**

1. **`KR-CONTR-2026-09` §13 shows contradiction is `K2`**
rows.statement: States as an argued verdict that the Gita supplies zero kernel candidates: KR-CONTR-2026-09 §13 already classifies contradiction as K2 (derivable from existing candidate powers, needing new representation not new capability); C-1 (do not add mechanisms to the kernel merely because they can be used) applies since textual resonance is a weaker warrant than usability, which already fails; the constitutional ban forbids the required derivation chain; and across the whole corpus the Gita's productive contribution has consistently been questions and lenses, never entities -- even the one derivation it helped motivate (the Zero/Sunya chain) was earned by 1,620,000 assignments, not by the reading.

rows.anchor: **Not** that corroboration from outside strengthens a KnowledgeOS result. **It does not.** A result derived from 20 000 trials and a deterministic witness suite is exactly as strong after this document as before it.
rows.statement: Explicitly warns against five conclusions this document must not be read as supporting: that the Gita supports four-valued logic, that visada should become a state/value/type, that dvandva-atita is an operator or φ should be derived from it, that outside corroboration strengthens a KnowledgeOS result (it does not -- a result's strength is unchanged by outside agreement), or that the absence of kernel candidates is a failure rather than the study's most disciplined output.

rows.anchor: > A philosophical text is **corroboration at best and decoration at worst.** It earns its place here by making one distinction askable that the programme then settled by proof
rows.statement: Closes by restating the governing rule (the strongest statement made must never exceed the strength of available evidence) and characterizing a philosophical text's proper epistemic role in this programme as corroboration at best, decoration at worst -- earning its place by making a distinction askable that the programme then settled independently by proof.

rows.anchor: > **Implement the candidate evaluation mechanism, not "FDE as KnowledgeOS logic."**
rows.statement: States the binding implementation boundary: implement the candidate evaluation mechanism (Standing(p)=(S+,S-)) as an experiment, never 'FDE as KnowledgeOS logic' -- Theory v1.2 remains unchanged regardless of implementation outcome.

Designs Standing(positive,negative) as an experimental representation strictly separate from a Boundary(facet,condition,context,provenance) record, explicitly rejecting a TRUE/FALSE/BOTH/NEITHER enum as a KnowledgeOS domain primitive (which would prematurely turn Priest's semantic values into ontology) -- the separation matters because (0,0) alone could mean no-evidence, not-assessed, unobservable, underdetermined, or theory-incomplete, and FDE cannot distinguish those on its own.

```text
ClassicalAdapter
K3Adapter
FDEAdapter
StructuredAdapter
```
rows.statement: Proposes implementing four experimental adapters (Classical, K3, FDE, Structured) rather than four KnowledgeOS domain states, tested against 14 named scenarios, measuring the pipeline required-distinction -> representation -> preserved?/collapsed?/reason-for-collapse -- distinction preservation, not value count, as the key metric.

rows.anchor:

rows.statement: Recommends implementing KR-CONTR-FDE-2026-09 as a sandboxed research module with a specific test-directory layout (scenarios/models/evaluators/invariants/witnesses/results/verdict.md), explicitly not touching the constitutional kernel, Theory v1.2, A_t, or production vocabulary; frames the precise question as whether independent positive/negative support plus an orthogonal boundary/reason dimension can preserve all currently-required Contr/Zero distinctions.

rows.anchor: The important thing is that **the adapters are competing representations**, not competing KnowledgeOS ontologies.
rows.statement: Reiterates that the four adapters (Classical, K3, FDE, Structured) must be implemented as competing representations under a shared EvaluationModel interface, never as competing KnowledgeOS ontologies -- FDE tests the lower semantic layer, Structured tests whether that layer needs additional dimensions.

rows.anchor: Record: preserved, collapsed, indeterminate, not representable, and, critically: collapse witness.
rows.statement: Specifies the distinction matrix should never reduce to YES/NO; each cell must record preserved/collapsed/indeterminate/not-representable plus a collapse witness (e.g. Unobservable≡NoEvidence≡NotAssessed under FDE) -- an experimental counterexample, not merely a score.

Reiterates the detector-not-definition discipline: implement fdeConflict as FDEConflictDetector, then test FDEConflict(p)≡?Contr(p) across the required distinction set, since FDE representing a glut/both condition does not establish that KnowledgeOS epistemic contradiction is identical to it.

rows.statement: Expands the design to require testing composition explicitly (e.g. E1 supports P, E2 supports not-P should produce Standing(P)=(1,1) only if the selected composition rule says so, and that rule itself must be an experimental candidate, not assumed) across single-evidence, contradictory-evidence, supersession, source-weighting, and temporal-separation cases -- preparing for the later composition experiment.

Establishes an architectural boundary where Zero becomes a downstream consumer of Evaluation (built from Standing + Boundary/Composition), never part of FDE itself: FDE-like Standing≠Boundary≠Zero, since FDE's 'neither' cannot tell us why a proposition lacks support.

rows.statement: Details the Structured model's two acceptable collapses: C1 (scenarios 4/5, No Evidence vs Not Assessed, both (0,0) but distinguished by Reason) and C2 (scenarios 3,8,12,13,14, all (1,1) contradiction-family cases distinguished by Reason/Provenance rather than by distinct S+/S- values) -- framed as evidence that a value channel should not be overloaded with type distinctions belonging in boundary metadata.

rows.statement: Supplies five worked countermodels demonstrating specific information loss: Classical cannot distinguish contradiction from logical impossibility/evaluation failure; K3 cannot distinguish genuine contradiction from epistemic uncertainty; FDE cannot distinguish why a contradiction exists (direct evidence conflict vs disagreeing sources, relevant to resolution strategy); K3/FDE cannot distinguish no-evidence-after-exhaustive-search (which may inform belief) from not-yet-assessed (which cannot); all three value-only models lose the temporal status of superseded vs current evidence.

rows.statement: States a Boundary-Value Separation invariant: values and boundary metadata must be kept separate, since values carry standing while boundary metadata carries the reasons for that standing; FDE violates it by collapsing contradiction type into B, K3 violates it by collapsing absence into U.

rows.statement: States Contr(p) iff S+(p)=1 and S-(p)=1 as a settled definition (with contradiction type given by R(p)) -- this directly conflicts with the main lane's KR-CONTR-EVAL-2026-09 (S2495 §15) finding that Pos∧Neg is necessary but not sufficient for Contr, since it over-generates (misclassifying retraction and supersession as contradiction) and requires an additional frame/currency qualifier phi; this document does not test or mention that requirement.
