rationale_evidence.statement: Specifies the four candidate representations to test fairly: A) extend {T,F,U} to {T,F,U,C}, testing whether C is primitive/derivable/needs provenance or polarity/can coexist with U; B) keep Sat in {T,F,U} and represent Contr(p,K) as an independent relation outside Sat; C) exclusive-by-construction (bot ≡ not-p∈K ∧ p∉K), explicitly flagged as expected-vulnerable to silently converting contradictory into false/absent/invalid; D) a structured EVal=(value,reason,provenance,evidence,context,time,polarity) tuple whose exact fields must be discovered by reduction.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Arjuna's state at 1.28–47 is: **not uncertainty**...**not absence**...**not insufficient evidence**...**not unobservability**...**not non-assessment**
rationale_evidence.statement: Analyzes Arjuna's viṣāda (Gita 1.28-47) as independently arriving, roughly 2000 years earlier, at exactly the KR-CONTR-2026-09 protocol's required-distinction list: his state is not uncertainty, not absence, not insufficient evidence, not unobservability, and not non-assessment -- corroboration of the distinctions, not evidence for any representation of them.

rationale_evidence.anchor: > **Four of ten findings get nothing from the text, and the two most technically load-bearing are among them.** That is the expected shape of an honest corroboration study.
rationale_evidence.statement: Tabulates a ten-row corroboration map against KR-CONTR-2026-09 findings, explicitly noting four rows (including 'minimum structure is a pair containing reason' and 'χ ranges 3-21', the two most technically load-bearing) get no textual support at all -- offered as evidence the study is reading the text honestly rather than reading itself into it.

rationale_evidence.anchor:
> ## **The Gītā supplies NO kernel candidate. Not one.**

1. **`KR-CONTR-2026-09` §13 shows contradiction is `K2`**
rationale_evidence.statement: States as an argued verdict that the Gita supplies zero kernel candidates: KR-CONTR-2026-09 §13 already classifies contradiction as K2 (derivable from existing candidate powers, needing new representation not new capability); C-1 (do not add mechanisms to the kernel merely because they can be used) applies since textual resonance is a weaker warrant than usability, which already fails; the constitutional ban forbids the required derivation chain; and across the whole corpus the Gita's productive contribution has consistently been questions and lenses, never entities -- even the one derivation it helped motivate (the Zero/Sunya chain) was earned by 1,620,000 assignments, not by the reading.

single_candidate_flags.why_uncertain: Invariant Custody is named as a distinct concept within the structure-first framework in prior batches; unclear whether it already has its own index entry distinct from the parent principle or is being named here for the first time as a sub-concept.

Invariant custody appears here as an already 'well-defined' derived result, but S2478 (same batch, same day) lists formalizing invariant custody as an open sub-todo (H3); unclear whether these are the same object at different maturity, or two different framings that need reconciliation.

sources.note: Cross-experiment diagnosis and reframing: the programme's five failures all stem from defining a projection (Sat_c, Zero<=>Delta=empty, Gap, DetectGap, K_t=Gamma(E_t)) and asking it to do the work of the structure it projects from; recommends defining the structure first and deriving the projection. Recurs through later files in this batch (hpa rulings, restructuring proposal).

rows.anchor: The programme has repeatedly defined a projection and then asked it to do the work of the structure it projects from. ... Each time, the information the theory needed was in the kernel of the projection.
rows.statement: Cross-experiment diagnosis: five apparently separate failures (Sat_c:=value∘Eval_c collapsing 9 evaluation situations into U; Zero<=>Delta=empty naming three disagreeing predicates; Gap=pi_Q(boundary) attribute-lossy; DetectGap derivable from ZeroLens; Gamma cannot be factive because its domain excludes truth) are one repeated structural mistake: defining a projection and asking it to do the work of the structure it projects from, with the needed information sitting in the projection's kernel each time.

rows.anchor: M-1. DEF-1 factivity and K = Gamma(E,Q,C,EC) are jointly unsatisfiable. ... 420 violations / 10 000 paired worlds ... Not established: that KnowledgeOS should be non-factive.
rows.statement: M-1: DEF-1 factivity and K=Gamma(E,Q,C,EC) are jointly unsatisfiable, witnessed by two worlds differing only in truth value producing a bit-identical epistemic state and hence an identical K that is true in one world and false in the other; reproduced at scale (420/10000 paired worlds), and the only escaping Gamma attributes nothing; explicitly NOT establishing that KnowledgeOS should be non-factive.

rows.anchor: M-2. Minimality is representation-relative. |K_min| = 13 under one algebra, 8 under another. ... A minimality claim without a fixed admissible algebra is not a claim.
rows.statement: M-2: kernel minimality is representation-relative (|K_min|=13 under one algebra, 8 under another are solutions to different optimization problems, not conflicting measurements); a minimality claim without a fixed admissible algebra is not a claim.

rows.anchor: any operator is a KnowledgeOS primitive: not established ... the eight requirement classes are exhaustive: untestable ... the reason vocabulary is exhaustive: [OPEN] ... Zero ∈ 𝒦: NOT TESTED ... the boundary is formally complete: [OPEN] -- 37 of 41 typed distinctions rest on provenance alone.
rows.statement: Table of claims that are NOT established and should stop being asserted: no operator is a settled KnowledgeOS primitive (DetectGap is the only settled case, settled negatively); the eight requirement classes' exhaustiveness is untestable; the reason vocabulary's exhaustiveness is [OPEN]; Zero-in-Kernel is NOT TESTED; and boundary formal completeness is [OPEN], with 37 of 41 typed distinctions resting on provenance alone.

rows.anchor: D-1. The constitutional four-layer separation. v1.2's ban on philosophy -> mathematics -> primitive -> DDD object -> architecture held under pressure. ... corroboration ≠ derivation is doing real work.
rows.statement: D-1: the constitutional four-layer separation (banning philosophy->mathematics->primitive->DDD object->architecture collapse) held under pressure across the eleven experiments -- Buddhi, Sarathi and Zero remained lenses, the Gita tiering placed zero new primitives, and the one item reaching the kernel question (Zero-as-non-collapse) was tested rather than promoted; 'corroboration != derivation' is doing real work.

rows.anchor: D-2. The distinctions the theory declares are operationally real. ... Evidence ≠ Knowledge · Determination ≠ Knowledge · Reject ≠ Accept · the four-way unknown taxonomy · and the full decision lane ... each adjacent pair separated by an explicit counterexample. Zero fabrications in 10 000 trials.
rows.statement: D-2: under adversarial test, the theory's declared distinctions (Evidence!=Knowledge, Determination!=Knowledge, Reject!=Accept, the four-way unknown taxonomy, and the full decision lane Determination->Proposal->Decision->Authorization->Action) each held with an explicit counterexample separating adjacent pairs, with zero fabrications across 10,000 trials.

rows.anchor: D-3. Three notions of necessity, kept apart. Formal (no composition reproduces it), functional (the capability fails without it), and domain (a distinct responsibility) disagree -- for Discriminate, Select and Revise. Collapsing them would have produced a confident and wrong kernel.
rows.statement: D-3: three notions of operator necessity -- formal (no composition reproduces it), functional (the capability fails without it), and domain (a distinct responsibility) -- disagree for the Discriminate, Select and Revise operators; collapsing the three notions would have produced a confident and wrong kernel.

rows.anchor: D-4. Invariant custody. A reduction can shrink |𝒦| while increasing the number of operators whose removal breaks an invariant: eliminating Challenge moved custody of 'a verdict must be challengeable' from one operator to two. Cardinality minimization is blind to this.
rows.statement: D-4 (invariant custody): a kernel reduction can shrink |K| while increasing the number of operators whose removal breaks an invariant -- eliminating Challenge moved custody of the invariant 'a verdict must be challengeable' from one operator to two; cardinality minimization is blind to this redistribution of invariant custody.

rows.anchor: I-6. The status vocabulary needs one more term. It cannot express 'refuted as reading A, surviving as reading B,' which is exactly Zero's situation: refuted as a state and as a missingness representation, surviving as a derived view.
rows.statement: I-6: the corpus's status vocabulary lacks a term for 'refuted as reading A, surviving as reading B' -- exactly Zero's situation, refuted as a state and as a missingness representation, surviving as a derived view.

rows.anchor: The kernel cannot be selected, and the reason is not that the work is unfinished. ... A kernel selected now would be a selection of a representation, disguised as a discovery about knowledge.
rows.statement: Kernel membership is a question about operations; operation semantics (delta), equality (=,~,cong_lambda) and the closure predicate are all open (the closure predicate itself shown three-way ambiguous in -B), and THM-10 shows cardinality is representation-relative -- so a kernel selected now would be a selection of a representation disguised as a discovery about knowledge; the kernel question is hard not because the answer is elusive but because it was asked first.

rows.anchor: ABANDON: define the projection, then try to recover the structure from it. ADOPT: define the structure, then derive the projection. ... Every one of the five failures in Part I is an instance of the abandoned direction.
rows.statement: Central reframing recommendation: ABANDON defining a projection first and trying to recover structure from it; ADOPT defining the structure first (Eval_c(K,r,Gamma)->EVal; the boundary B(K,I,Gamma,L); the epistemic state's type) and deriving the projection (Sat_c; Gap/Zero/U; K_t=Gamma(E_t,...)) from it -- every one of the five Part-I failures instantiates the abandoned direction.

rows.anchor: What mathematical structure must an epistemic state preserve under all admissible representations and transitions? ... It is hard because it was asked first.
rows.statement: The question worth reopening: what mathematical structure must an epistemic state preserve under all admissible representations and transitions? The kernel-membership question (which operators belong to the kernel) is shown to be downstream of at least four others: the type of K_t, the definition of semantic equivalence, the contradiction predicate, and the status ordering.

rows.anchor: This does not reorder the agreed path. Factivity → Contr → ⪰ stands ... But it does say that ⪰ is the item with the largest existing debt attached to it. ... Declare the lens register ... Decide whether Δ is a count or an ordered quantity ... Do not attempt to define ⪰ by choosing a metric on gap counts.
rows.statement: Confirms the existing Factivity->Contr->(status ordering) research priority is unchanged, but quantifies that the status ordering carries the largest existing debt; proposes two cheap parallel next steps (declare the lens register; decide whether Delta is a count or an ordered quantity) while explicitly warning not to define the status ordering by merely choosing a metric on gap counts, since a count structurally cannot make the needed distinction.

rows.anchor: We repeatedly tried to make a reduced representation answer questions that only the richer structure could answer. ... A representation cannot recover distinctions that its projection has identified. That is a mathematical statement, not merely an architectural preference.
rows.statement: Sharpens the batch's structure-over-projection diagnosis into a precise mathematical statement: a representation cannot recover distinctions its projection has identified, unifying failures across Sat, Zero, Gap, Balanced, K_t, and the argument field (B->U loses the boundary reason; AF->Balanced loses relation type; E->K may lose factivity-relevant distinctions).

rows.anchor: For a general semantic map π:X→Y we should not automatically call something the kernel. The rigorous object is the induced equivalence: x_1 ~_π x_2 iff π(x_1)=π(x_2). ... Every projection must declare which distinctions it identifies. That should replace 'every projection declares its kernel.'
rows.statement: Corrects the informal 'information in the kernel of the projection' language: the rigorous object for a map pi:X->Y is the induced equivalence relation x1~_pi x2 iff pi(x1)=pi(x2) (creating equivalence classes [x]_pi), replacing the principle 'every projection declares its kernel' with 'every projection must declare which distinctions it identifies.'

rows.anchor: ZeroLens(𝒮,π) = examination of distinctions hidden by π. ... This is potentially much stronger than: Zero=unknown or: Zero ⟺ Δ=∅. The latter has already been retired by our experiments.
rows.statement: Proposes reinterpreting Zero mathematically as ZeroLens(S,pi) = examination of the distinctions hidden by a projection pi, superseding both 'Zero=unknown' and the already-retired 'Zero iff Delta=empty' definitions.

rows.anchor: It is not enough to ask: |R_2|<|R_1|? We must ask: Which invariants survived? And more importantly: Who owns each invariant after reduction? ... elimination of an operator is admissible only if every required invariant retains an explicit owner. ... Custody_after(I) ≠ ∅ for every invariant I.
rows.statement: Generalizes invariant custody (from the eleven-experiments synthesis, D-4) into a formal reduction criterion: a representation reduction R1->R2 is admissible only if Custody_after(I) is non-empty for every invariant I the eliminated structure was responsible for -- cardinality reduction alone (|R2|<|R1|) is insufficient justification.

rows.anchor: Kernel status = NOT SELECTABLE because semantic equivalence has not been established. The proper sequence becomes: Structure → Observables → Semantic Equivalence → Invariant Preservation → Reduction → Minimality. ... Cardinality is representation-dependent.
rows.statement: Reaffirms kernel status as NOT SELECTABLE pending semantic equivalence, proposing a corrected methodological sequence Structure->Observables->SemanticEquivalence->InvariantPreservation->Reduction->Minimality, explicitly forbidding 'fewer operators = better/minimal' reasoning since cardinality is representation-dependent.

rows.anchor: A_t=Γ(E_t,Q,C,EC) is a useful repair. But we should not yet conclude: Factivity = external. ... DEF-1 + K_t=Γ(E_t,...) was jointly unsatisfiable under the tested model. Therefore: Externalization = candidate architectural decision not: Externalization = discovered theoretical truth.
rows.statement: Cautions against over-generalizing the R2 externalized-factivity repair: the experiment established only that DEF-1 factivity and K_t=Gamma(E_t,...) are jointly unsatisfiable under the tested model, so externalizing factivity is a candidate architectural decision, not a discovered theoretical truth.

rows.anchor: E_t, 𝓑_t, AF_t, M_t = candidate primary structures not: E_t, 𝓑_t, AF_t, M_t = the primary structures. ... we have not yet demonstrated that 𝓑_t cannot be derived from another structure. Likewise AF_t could be relational structure over other objects.
rows.statement: Insists the four proposed 'primary structures' (Evidence, Boundary, ArgumentField, Model) remain candidates, not settled primitives, since none has been shown underivable from another structure.

rows.anchor: For every projection π_i, determine: 1. Information loss ... 2. Induced equivalence ... 3. Recoverability ... 4. Invariant preservation ... 5. Adequacy ... This could become the mathematical backbone of the next phase of KnowledgeOS research.
rows.statement: Proposes a unifying five-question research programme applicable to every projection in the theory (Sat, Zero, Gap, Balanced, K, kernel operators): information loss, induced equivalence, recoverability, invariant preservation, and adequacy -- offered as the mathematical backbone of the next research phase.

rows.anchor: KR-PROJ-2026-09-02 -- Projection, Information Loss and Invariant Preservation ... I agree. In fact, after reading the complete document, I would make it the clear next gate. ... The experiment should try to falsify: E_t,𝓑_t,AF_t,M_t as candidate primary structures.
rows.statement: Endorses KR-PROJ-2026-09-02 (Projection, Information Loss and Invariant Preservation) as the clear next research gate, specifying it should attempt to falsify the four candidate primary structures via seven per-candidate questions (what evidence requires it; derivability from another candidate; distinctions preserved/lost; dependent invariants; alternative custody; necessity vs convenience), distinguishing necessary structure from useful representation.

rows.anchor: ESTABLISHED/strong: Projection can destroy distinctions ... PROPOSED: structure-first architecture ... E_t,𝓑_t,AF_t,M_t as candidate primary structures ... representation-adequacy principle ... OPEN: semantic equivalence, Contr, ≽, ... RETIRED: Zero⟺Δ=∅. Theory v1.3 does not exist yet.
rows.statement: Produces a comprehensive four-category research status ledger: ESTABLISHED/strong (9 items including projection-can-destroy-distinctions, Sat/U/Balanced/Gap lossiness, semantic-equivalence-before-minimality, invariant custody, lens/domain separation), PROPOSED (8 items including the structure-first architecture, the four candidate primary structures, the projection/information-loss framework, the representation-adequacy principle, candidate ClosureEvent), OPEN (11 items including semantic equivalence, Contr, the status ordering, temporal semantics, kernel selection), and RETIRED (Zero iff Delta=empty) -- reaffirming Theory v1.3 does not yet exist.

rows.anchor: This is the most important document in the entire KnowledgeOS reconstruction. It establishes a general mathematical theory of what KnowledgeOS loses when it compresses knowledge representations -- a principle that unifies Sat, Zero, Gap, Balanced, K, and every other failure we have encountered.
rows.statement: Formal HPA Supervisory ruling declares the structure-first/projection framework (from S2463) 'the most important document in the entire KnowledgeOS reconstruction' and formally ACCEPTS it as the confirmed research path, status [PROP] Very Strong pending KR-PROJ.

rows.anchor: Layer 0: Lenses (Zero, Yoni, Lord, Sārathi) -- Instruments, never domain objects. Layer 1: Structures (E_t, 𝓑_t, AF_t, M_t) -- Candidate primary structures. Layer 2: Projections (Sat, Gap, U, Zero, Balanced) -- All derived, none primitive. Layer 3: Attribution (A_t = Γ(E_t,Q,C,EC)) -- Not knowledge. Layer 4: Transition + Event -- δ:E_t→E_{t+1}. Layer 5: History -- Append-only, written by kernel.
rows.statement: Proposes a six-layer candidate architecture: Layer 0 Lenses (instruments, never domain objects), Layer 1 Structures (candidate primary structures E_t/B_t/AF_t/M_t), Layer 2 Projections (Sat/Gap/U/Zero/Balanced, all derived, none primitive), Layer 3 Attribution (not knowledge), Layer 4 Transition+Event, Layer 5 History (append-only, kernel-written).

rows.anchor: L1 No projection is primitive [PROP] Very Strong. L2 Every projection declares its kernel [PROP] Very Strong. L3 Kernel writes history, never reads [PROP] Conditional. L4 Lens never on RHS of domain equation [PROP] Strong. L5 Every claim of progress names its ordering [PROP] Very Strong.
rows.statement: Names and status-ranks four (five-numbered, L1-L5) structural laws: L1 no projection is primitive, L2 every projection declares its kernel/identified distinctions, L3 the kernel writes history and never reads it (marked Conditional, reflecting S2463's caution), L4 a lens never appears on the right-hand side of a domain equation, L5 every progress claim must name its ordering.

rows.anchor: KR-PROJ-2026-09-02 ... Success Criterion: All previously observed failures can be explained as projection-induced information loss. Failure Criterion: Some observed failure cannot be explained by projection-induced information loss.
rows.statement: Formally commissions KR-PROJ-2026-09-02 with an explicit binary success/failure criterion: success if all previously observed corpus failures can be explained as projection-induced information loss, failure if any cannot -- with the critical rule 'do not assume Claude's four structures are correct; let the experiment try to falsify them.'

rows.anchor: Old Chain (Retired): Operators → Count → Minimum → Kernel. New Chain: Structure → Observables → Semantic Equivalence → Invariant Preservation → Reduction → Minimality.
rows.statement: Explicitly retires the old dependency chain (Operators->Count->Minimum->Kernel) in favor of the corrected chain (Structure->Observables->SemanticEquivalence->InvariantPreservation->Reduction->Minimality).

rows.anchor: 'The document establishes a general mathematical theory...' I would not say that yet. What has been established is: A very strong explanatory hypothesis has emerged: many KnowledgeOS failures can be explained as projection-induced information loss. That is different from having established a general theory.
rows.statement: Corrects the structure-first document's self-description as having 'established a general mathematical theory': what is actually established is a strong explanatory hypothesis (many failures explainable as projection-induced information loss), which is weaker than a general theory.

rows.anchor: The experiment should be allowed to discover: 2 structures, 3 structures, 4 structures, 5 structures, a different decomposition, or even that 'structure' itself needs another formulation. That is scientifically cleaner.
rows.statement: Reinforces that KR-PROJ must not presuppose exactly four candidate structures; the experiment should be free to discover any number or a different decomposition entirely, or that 'structure' itself needs reformulation.

rows.anchor: Structure → Representation → Projection → Boundary → Inquiry → Candidate Generation → Evaluation → Transition with the lenses sitting outside this chain: EXTERNAL LENSES [Yoni→generation, Zero→boundary, Sārathi→guidance, Lord→candidate-making] → STRUCTURE → PROJECTION → INDUCED EQUIVALENCE → INFORMATION LOSS → INVARIANT CUSTODY → ADEQUACY.
rows.statement: Proposes a corrected combined architecture merging the structure-first chain with the lens vocabulary: Structure->Representation->Projection->Boundary->Inquiry->CandidateGeneration->Evaluation->Transition, with all four lenses (Yoni/generation, Zero/boundary, Sarathi/guidance, Lord/candidate-making) placed explicitly outside/above this chain as external instruments feeding it, rather than being nodes within it.

rows.anchor: We have not discovered the KnowledgeOS kernel. What we have discovered is something potentially more fundamental: Before reducing KnowledgeOS, we must understand what every representation destroys. ... Yoni and Zero should remain lenses that generate and inspect hypotheses about that programme, not architectural primitives.
rows.statement: States the overall research-state summary: the KnowledgeOS kernel has not been discovered, but the more fundamental prerequisite has been found -- before reducing KnowledgeOS, one must understand what every representation destroys; Yoni and Zero remain lenses generating/inspecting hypotheses about that programme, not architectural primitives, and KR-PROJ is endorsed as the correct next step over implementing the Yoni-Zero engine.

Reality → Observation → Evidence → Interpretation → Hypotheses → Assessment → Determination → Knowledge Attribution → K_t and then: K_t → Ideal State → Gap/Zero → Proposal → Decision → Action → Observation_{t+1} → K_{t+1}.
rows.statement: States the overall assessment that KnowledgeOS Theory v1.2 is a strong research/architectural theory but not a final theory, summarized by two chained pipelines: Reality->Observation->Evidence->Interpretation->Hypotheses->Assessment->Determination->KnowledgeAttribution->K_t, followed by K_t->IdealState->Gap/Zero->Proposal->Decision->Action->Observation_{t+1}->K_{t+1}.

rows.anchor: Knowledge ≠ probability, Knowledge ≠ information, Knowledge ≠ evidence, Knowledge ≠ belief, Knowledge ≠ determination, Knowledge ≠ selected hypothesis, Knowledge ≠ balanced arguments, Zero ≠ simply 'missing data', Zero ≠ probability zero, Closure ≠ a permanent state, candidate count ≠ epistemic complexity, validation ≠ truth, selection + validation ≠ knowledge, fit ≠ causal validity, representation equality ≠ semantic equality, more observations ≠ necessarily better knowledge, more hypotheses ≠ necessarily better knowledge, scalar cancellation ≠ reconciliation, external philosophical metaphors ≠ KnowledgeOS architecture.
rows.statement: Catalogs the single most important discovery as negative: a list of nineteen falsified simplifications the programme has repeatedly eliminated (Knowledge!=probability/information/evidence/belief/determination/selected-hypothesis/balanced-arguments; Zero!=missing-data/probability-zero; Closure!=permanent state; candidate-count!=complexity; validation!=truth; selection+validation!=knowledge; fit!=causal validity; representation-equality!=semantic-equality; more-observations/hypotheses!=necessarily-better-knowledge; scalar-cancellation!=reconciliation; external-metaphors!=architecture) -- framed as real theoretical progress, since a theory strengthens by eliminating plausible-but-false propositions.

rows.anchor: K_t ≠ K_{t+1}. Knowledge is represented as a changing state, while historical identity and transition history are separate concerns. This is one of our strongest foundations.
rows.statement: Lists K_t as a time-indexed changing epistemic state (K_t!=K_{t+1}, with historical identity/transition history kept separate) as one of the theory's strongest and most stable foundations.

rows.anchor: Q=(Target,Purpose,Context,Requirements,...) determines what counts as adequate. Therefore: Adequacy(K_t,Q,C,EC) is inquiry-relative. This is a major conceptual result.
rows.statement: Reaffirms inquiry-relative adequacy as a major stable conceptual result: the system has no context-free 'enough knowledge' notion; adequacy Adequacy(K_t,Q,C,EC) is always relative to the inquiry tuple Q=(Target,Purpose,Context,Requirements,...).

rows.anchor: Knows(a,p,c,t) ⇒ True(p,c,t) but the simulator showed that an epistemic state cannot determine external truth merely from its internal contents. ... A models knowledge itself, which must be factive, or B models an epistemic state containing claims, beliefs, hypotheses, assessments, etc., with a separate attribution layer for knowledge. Our experiments strongly point toward B.
rows.statement: Restates factivity as the most serious unresolved theoretical problem: the desired Knows(a,p,c,t)=>True(p,c,t) cannot be satisfied because an epistemic state cannot determine external truth from internal contents alone, forcing a choice between Model A (KnowledgeOS models factive knowledge itself) and Model B (it models a broader epistemic state with a separate knowledge-attribution layer) -- experiments strongly favor B, but the theory has not yet formalized this properly.

rows.anchor: R_1 ≡_sem R_2 based on contract-relevant observable behavior. But the definition risks circularity: 'They are semantically equivalent if they have the same semantic behavior.' We need a non-circular formalization. And this matters because kernel minimality depends on it.
rows.statement: Restates the semantic-equivalence problem as possibly the deepest open mathematical problem: candidate definitions of R1 =_sem R2 based on contract-relevant observable behavior risk circularity ('equivalent if they have the same semantic behavior'), and a non-circular formalization is required precisely because kernel minimality depends on it.

rows.anchor: the original candidate kernel was too small; DetectGap can be derived; 14 irreducible powers appeared under one representation; 12 irreducible operators; two minimal kernels had the same cardinality; further reduction became unstable under semantic granularity changes. ... Kernel minimality cannot be decided merely by counting operators. It requires: fixed carrier + capabilities + observable behavior + semantic equivalence + invariant preservation.
rows.statement: Summarizes the kernel-minimality research trajectory (original candidate too small; DetectGap derivable; 14 then 12 irreducible-power counts under different representations; two same-cardinality minimal kernels; instability under semantic-granularity changes) into the methodological conclusion that kernel minimality cannot be decided by operator-counting alone, requiring fixed carrier + capabilities + observable behavior + semantic equivalence + invariant preservation together.

rows.anchor: EA(E,H,𝓗,M,S,C) → Standing(H) where assessment depends on: evidence, competing hypotheses, model, assumptions, epistemic standards, context, dependence structure. That is much richer than simply: P(H|E). So Bayesian probability is one regime inside KnowledgeOS, not the KnowledgeOS epistemology itself.
rows.statement: Proposes Evidence Assessment needs its own formal theory beyond Bayesian P(H|E): EA(E,H,HypothesisSpace,Model,Standards,Context)->Standing(H), depending on evidence, competing hypotheses, model, assumptions, standards, context, and dependence structure; positions Bayesian probability as one regime inside KnowledgeOS, not the whole epistemology.

rows.anchor: I would NOT start another philosophical model now. ... The next phase should be: Theory consolidation and formal closure, not theory expansion. ... KnowledgeOS Theory v1.2 = Research Baseline not Final Theory.
rows.statement: Recommends against starting another philosophical model (Plato/Gita/Davidson/Dretske/Buddhist/Nyaya/etc.), citing diminishing returns; declares the next phase should be theory consolidation and formal closure rather than expansion, formally positioning KnowledgeOS Theory v1.2 as a Research Baseline, not a Final Theory.

rows.anchor: KnowledgeOS Theory v2.0 -- Formal Closure with only the minimum remaining questions: 1. What exactly is K_t? 2. What exactly is Knowledge Attribution? 3. What exactly is Evidence Assessment? 4. What exactly is Zero? 5. What is semantic equivalence? 6. What is the minimal kernel under that equivalence? 7. Which invariants are actually proven/experimentally supported? 8. Which claims remain hypotheses?
rows.statement: Proposes the next research target as 'KnowledgeOS Theory v2.0 -- Formal Closure', reducing the remaining agenda to eight specific well-defined questions (exact nature of K_t, Knowledge Attribution, Evidence Assessment, Zero, semantic equivalence, the resulting minimal kernel, which invariants are proven vs hypothesized) -- if answerable without introducing further conceptual layers, a genuinely final theory may be achievable.

rows.anchor: Do not put statistical mechanisms into the kernel merely because KnowledgeOS can use them. For example: candidate generation, hypothesis selection, multiplicity control, correlation modelling, validation, Bayesian updating, may all be important capabilities of the system without being irreducible kernel operators.
rows.statement: States a general kernel-discipline principle: statistical mechanisms useful to KnowledgeOS (candidate generation, hypothesis selection, multiplicity control, correlation modelling, validation, Bayesian updating) need not be irreducible kernel operators -- the kernel should remain at the level of the smallest invariant epistemic powers.

rows.anchor: KR-PROJ says: x_1~_π x_2 ⟺ π(x_1)=π(x_2) ... Effective multiplicity may ultimately be a consequence of distinguishability/equivalence.
rows.statement: Proposes a structural parallel between KR-PROJ's induced-equivalence framework (x1~_pi x2 iff pi(x1)=pi(x2)) and KR-NEFF's candidate-space question (how many candidates are genuinely distinguishable under a regime), hypothesizing effective multiplicity may ultimately be a consequence of distinguishability/equivalence -- not yet aware of (or not referencing) the immediately-preceding KR-DIST experiment that tests and refutes exactly this construction.

rows.anchor: 'The most important document in the entire KnowledgeOS reconstruction.' I would soften that. The Structure-First hypothesis is currently the strongest unifying research direction, but KR-NEFF has now shown that there is another potentially fundamental axis: Representation distinguishability ↔ Hypothesis-space distinguishability. These may turn out to be two manifestations of the same underlying mathematical principle.
rows.statement: Softens the HPA ruling's (S2464) self-description of the structure-first document as 'the most important document in the entire KnowledgeOS reconstruction', proposing instead that Representation distinguishability and Hypothesis-space distinguishability may be two manifestations of one underlying mathematical principle, neither document alone being uniquely most important.

rows.anchor: Can distinguishability/equivalence provide a common mathematical basis for both projection-induced information loss and effective hypothesis complexity? ... whether the same notion of equivalence can explain the earlier Sat→U, Boundary→U, Balanced, and K failures. If that succeeds, then we may have something much more fundamental than either Zero, Yoni, Sat, or N_eff.
rows.statement: Proposes the unifying research question of whether distinguishability/equivalence provides a common mathematical basis for both projection-induced information loss (KR-PROJ) and effective hypothesis complexity (KR-NEFF), with a six-part test plan including whether the same equivalence notion explains the Sat->U, Boundary->U, Balanced, and K failures -- if successful, this would be more fundamental than Zero, Yoni, Sat, or N_eff individually, and would be the point to revisit the kernel question.

rows.anchor: So I would change our immediate research priority. I would not do: Yoni-Zero architectural integration. And I would also not immediately do: another N_eff formula search. Instead: [distinguishability/equivalence unification question].
rows.statement: Recommends against both Yoni-Zero architectural integration and another N_eff formula search as immediate priorities, instead proposing the distinguishability/equivalence unification question as the next research target.

rows.anchor: v1.2 is itself a weakening of v1.1, and that is its principal virtue. It made four moves: 1. A constitutional four-layer separation ... 2. An epistemic status vocabulary ... 3. rows.statement: Summarizes Theory v1.2 as a deliberate weakening of v1.1 (its principal virtue) via four moves: the constitutional four-layer separation with an explicit ban on Gita-concept->mathematical-concept->primitive->DDD-object->architecture inference; an eleven-value epistemic status vocabulary applied to every claim; reopening several v1.1-closed concepts (Observation, Zero, E_t!=K_t, Buddhi/Sarathi-as-lenses); and the three-valued class-indexed Sat predicate.

The experiment has **not established that yet**. Better:

rows.statement: Softens the Projection/Invariant framework's epistemic status: 'this may be the mathematical foundation of the kernel' is corrected to 'this is a candidate mathematical foundation ... must be tested', preserving the discipline that research direction is not established architecture.

rows.anchor: D-0's agreement was attributed to the readings testing only F and U. True but incomplete. The models are separable in isolation — one unrelated U anywhere in the state masks the difference completely, in any bucket.
rows.statement: Corrects and sharpens D-0's earlier finding: the models ARE separable in isolation, but one unrelated U anywhere in the epistemic state masks the difference completely in any bucket, because Zero_weak/Zero_kleene are existential quantifiers that absorb at U; with 5 of 8 Sat_c classes non-executable, this masking saturation is the normal regime, not an edge case -- the sixth instance of the recurring projection-vs-structure diagnosis, and the first found in the readings rather than a value or metric.

rows.anchor: > The model's single claim is this: **every time the programme got stuck, it was holding a projection and looking for the structure. Hold the structure, and the projections come for free.**
rows.statement: States the proposal's honest summary and single claim: every time the programme got stuck it was holding a projection and looking for the structure -- hold the structure and the projections come for free; explicitly warns against adopting the model merely because experiments were successful (three stable results are not a threshold) and against repairing open items by implementation rather than specification.

rows.anchor:
For an arbitrary projection $$\pi:X\rightarrow Y,$$ there isn't necessarily a "kernel" in the algebraic sense. The better mathematical object is the **induced equivalence relation**: $$
x_1\sim_\pi x_2
\iff
\pi(x_1)=\pi(x_2).
$$
rows.statement: The review's central mathematical correction: 'kernel of a projection' is imprecise for an arbitrary non-algebraic projection π:X->Y; the correct object is the induced equivalence relation x1~_π x2 iff π(x1)=π(x2), giving Y≅X/~_π under appropriate conditions -- the rule should read 'every projection declares what distinctions it identifies', not 'declares its kernel'.

Strengthens L2 using the induced-equivalence-relation framing: the U-projection π_U:𝓑->{U} identifies every pair of boundary conditions as equivalent (b1~b2 for all b1,b2), which mathematically explains why Unknown and Contradiction can both collapse to U -- stronger than merely saying 'the projection loses information'.

rows.anchor:
We could study these as a family of maps: $$
\Pi=\{\pi_1,\pi_2,\ldots,\pi_n\}.
$$ ...Then ask: Which distinctions are destroyed by each projection?
rows.statement: Proposes studying the whole family of KnowledgeOS projections (E_t->K_t->A_t->Answer_Q; 𝓑_t->Gap->Zero; AF_t->Balanced) together as a projection family Π={π1..πn}, each inducing its own equivalence relation, asking systematically which distinctions each destroys -- a candidate rigorous mathematical framework for the whole programme.

Gives Zero a real mathematical interpretation without making it a state producer: ZeroLens(K,Π) analyzes distinctions lost by a projection π:E->K by examining the equivalence class [x]_π={e∈E : π(e)=π(x)} -- if a large equivalence class contains materially different epistemic states, the projection is hiding distinctions.

Reinterprets Yoni as remaining strictly [EXT] (never equalling a kernel/state/bounded-context) while the underlying mathematical abstraction becomes a candidate space with relations and transformations (H,R,Θ); likewise reinterprets Linga as an interpretive metaphor for a candidate-generation function G:K_t×Q_t->H_t, never Linga=G, yielding the pipeline Linga-like->Generation->CandidateSpace->Assessment->Selection->Transformation with ZeroLens examining the representation boundary.

Proposes a tentative post-review research architecture S_t --πi--> R_i,t (a candidate rich structure with a family of representations/projections), with ZeroLens(S_t,πi) examining lost distinctions and Θ:S_t×Input_t->S_{t+1} defining transformation separately from History_t recording it -- yielding the five-way separation Structure≠Projection≠Lens≠Transformation≠History.

States the review's bottom-line meta-principle: do not ask a projection to preserve distinctions its definition already discarded; the sharper mathematical successor is to define the structure, define the projection, define the induced equivalence, then test which invariants survive -- proposed as the next experiment ahead of Contr, ⪰, or kernel selection.

rows.anchor:
> ### A reading must be a function of `𝒮_t`.
> If it is computed from a projection `π` for efficiency, `π` must be **reading-complete** for it:
> ```
>          ρ factors through π      ⟺      ~_π  refines  ~_ρ
> ```
> **This is decidable and testable.**
rows.statement: States the new 'saturation law': a reading rho must be a function of the full state S_t; if computed via a projection pi for efficiency, pi must be reading-complete for it (rho factors through pi iff the equivalence relation induced by pi refines that induced by rho, iff pi(s1)=pi(s2) implies rho(s1)=rho(s2)) -- a decidable, testable criterion applying the induced-equivalence-relation rule to readings rather than to values.

The first is the model. The second is why anything in it can be believed.
rows.statement: Closes with the two sentences said to carry the most weight in the whole document: 'every projection declares what distinctions it identifies' (the model) and 'the strongest statement made must never exceed the strength of the available evidence' (why anything in the model can be believed).

sources.note: Step 114: the strict empirical test operationalizing Step 113 hypothesis. Per-concept T(C) evidence function and S0-S5 grading (S1 does not imply S5); worked through all eight core concepts with concrete gap-revealing experiments (Recommendation-vs-Decision, Authority-vs-role, ActionProvenance=Partial, etc); relationship-level semantic edge test and the Relationship-semantics-vs-foreign-keys distinction; semantic lifecycle/invariant tests with SpecifiedInvariant-vs-ImplementedInvariant; the target Authority->Decision->Action->Observation->Evidence feedback chain; explicit warning against premature architecture claims; the formal semantic-core evidence matrix and ordinal Grade(C) 0-6 scale; the deliberately-deferred SemanticCoreStrength score with Vector>Scalar principle; semantic completeness as edge-presence and Core_minimum; the decisive Knowledge-Retrieval-Platform vs Knowledge-Operating-System distinction with a full feedback-loop diagram; DelegatedAuthority for autonomous agents; ModelOutput vs DecisionEvidence; the KnowledgeOS identity/fragmentation test; and the symmetric two-strongest-findings framing. Verdict: ConceptualSemanticCore!=ProvenActualSemanticCore, READY FOR EMPIRICAL EXECUTION. Extends knowledgeos-semantic-core-model (S1012); previews Step 115 semantic graph reconstruction.
